overview: This file consists of two State Department cross-reference records, one with an attached fragmentary copy, concerning Japan’s cement industry between 1930 and 1932. The 1930 material reports that the Temporary Industrial Nationalization Bureau considered rationalizing the Cement Federation and the wider cement industry, including a possible merger of companies. The 1932 reference points to a report describing current conditions in the Japanese cement industry as unsatisfactory, despite the industry’s reputedly sound condition; the substantive telegrams were filed elsewhere in the decimal file.

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: U.S. diplomatic officer in Japan and sender of the referenced telegrams; precise position is not stated in these documents

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to telegram no. 219 on rationalization of the cement industry
subfiles.about: The sheet redirects researchers to telegram no. 219 concerning proposals to rationalize and consolidate Japan’s cement industry.
subfiles.summary: This filing note refers the reader to file 894.00 P.R./32 for telegram no. 219 from Neville in Japan. It records that the first meeting of a committee of the Temporary Industrial Nationalization Bureau considered rationalization of the Cement Federation and the cement industry, including a possible merger of companies. The note states that a copy was attached.

subfiles.title: Attached excerpt on Cement Federation rationalization
subfiles.about: This fragment reports a Bureau committee’s discussion of rationalizing the Cement Federation and merging cement companies.
subfiles.summary: The attached fragment repeats that a committee of the Bureau met to consider rationalization of the Cement Federation and its industry. It specifically notes discussion of a merger among companies. The text ends abruptly and is evidently only a partial copy or excerpt associated with the preceding cross-reference sheet.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to telegram no. 107 on conditions in the Japanese cement industry
subfiles.about: The sheet redirects researchers to a telegram reporting contradictory assessments of the Japanese cement industry’s condition.
subfiles.summary: This filing note refers the reader to section G of telegram no. 107, sent at 9 a.m., in file 894.50/62. The referenced report described current conditions in Japan’s cement industry as unsatisfactory, although the industry was generally supposed to be in good condition. No further statistical or explanatory detail appears on the sheet.

interest: The file is useful less for detailed industrial statistics than for tracing how information about Japan’s cement sector was classified and distributed across the State Department’s decimal filing system. It captures official interest in interwar Japanese industrial rationalization, cartel or federation organization, and corporate consolidation, while the 1932 item preserves a suggestive discrepancy between reported difficulties and the industry’s favorable reputation. The cross-references also direct historians to the locations of the fuller telegrams needed to reconstruct the underlying policy discussions.
